name: Liesegang Rings
desc: Periodic precipitation in a gel: reagent invades from a pipetted source, meets the loaded gel and reacts into a soluble product that stays clear until it passes supersaturation and suddenly drops out as a band - which strips the product back down, so the front must run on and re-supersaturate before it can band again, laying discrete rings of widening spacing rather than a smooth stain; new sources keep arriving so ring systems collide and interfere, read as ochre bands in translucent gel, banded agate, scattering rings in dark field, or a blueprint of contours.

energy.doc: contrast and colour gain of the precipitate bands

scale.doc: magnification into the plate - guaranteed visible change

speed.doc: diffusion and reaction rate - how fast the fronts invade (0.2 still bands)

density.doc: how often fresh sources are pipetted in, and how loaded the gel is - number of ring systems on the plate

spacing.doc: supersaturation threshold - wide spacing between few bold rings vs tight stacks of fine ones

hue.doc: hue of the precipitate; the gel takes a cool complement

x.doc: pan across the plate when magnified

y.doc: pan down the plate when magnified

style.doc: aesthetic: ochre bands suspended in translucent gel / polished banded agate slab / scattering rings on black / blueprint of band contours
